claims.claim_vi: Stage 1: Bob opens the chat app, a WebSocket is established; the pub-sub server opens several Redis connections (one to update data models and publish, others to subscribe); the client gets the member list and message history from Redis; a message is published to the member_add topic for a new member.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Stage 2: a new message is added to a Redis sorted set with zadd, sorted by arrival time, then published to the messages topic; the recipient's client receives it.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Own experiment, 2026-10-19, Redis 7.0.15 on one machine: an early subscriber received all 3 published messages, a late subscriber only the third; ZRANGE returned all 3 in order; PUBLISH to a channel with no subscriber returned 0; GET on a subscribed connection was refused with an error naming the allowed commands; ZADD of the same member twice kept one element with the later score; members of equal score came back in lexicographic order.
claims.verified_by: Commands run in the session with redis-server and redis-cli; results copied from their output.

claims.claim_vi: The lesson explains the separate connections and the non-persistence of pub/sub from the experiment, not from the Redis documentation.
claims.verified_by: Author's reasoning from the experiment; Author's general knowledge, not checked against the primary document in this session (the egress proxy allows GitHub only).

design_notes_vi: Khung một là sơ đồ trình tự ba bên; khung hai là hai ghi chú. Tên lệnh viết thường trong hình. Bảng thử nghiệm ở trong bài.
source_deviations: The source numbers eight initialisation steps and three message steps; the lesson groups them into two paragraphs.
The lesson adds an experiment table and the unique-member and late-subscriber pitfalls, none of which the source mentions.
